author: norm-paper-review
body: Started source review. Reading only original exposition.txt and the frozen contract; no Lean/source search or edits. Review scope: Lemma 8.6, equations (6.2), (6.6)-(6.7), and its stated C_y^m estimate.

author: norm-paper-review
body:
Source review (read-only; original .codex/state/norm-route-audit/exposition.txt, pdftotext line numbers; no Lean search).

Interpretation and arithmetic:
- PDF p.95, exposition.txt lines 4977–4983: Lemma 8.6 takes smooth F on T² of zero Haar mean, N=v_t·∂_y with v_t fixed by (6.2), and gives unique zero-mean solution with ||N^-1 F||_{C_y^m} ≤ C_m ||F||_{C_y^{m+4}} for every integer m≥0. The displayed Fourier sum is over nonzero k∈Z² and has denominator 2πi(v_t·k).
- PDF p.64, lines 3354–3366: (6.7) asserts |v_t·n|≥c/(1+|n|) for all nonzero integer n, with c fixed by the quadratic-irrational direction. Hence the inverse multiplier costs one frequency power. For a standard C^m torus norm, four extra derivatives leave a summable weight (1+|k|)^−3 in dimension two, exactly as the proof states (p.96, lines 5003–5005). The four-derivative loss is arithmetically consistent for this domain and this divisor bound; no excess/deficit is apparent.
- Uniformity: the displayed C_m is independent of F and its slow point, since N and its direction are fixed. The statement is pointwise in the other variables; (p.96, lines 5006–5008) says the multiplier commutes with slow coefficient derivatives and preserves slow/radial support and smooth zero extensions. In application, (6.6)–(6.7) give N_abs = T_g^i N_i and fast normalized derivative c_i N_i (p.63, lines 3319–3337; p.95, lines 4970–4975). Equations (8.20), (8.23) state the chart scaling and agreement across finite covers (p.96, lines 4990–4992, 5009–5015). It does not preserve auxiliary-torus support (p.96, lines 5007–5008). It acts in auxiliary y/Y, not in spatial torus directions.

Bounded search / unresolved convention:
- Searched the complete supplied exposition text for C_y^m/Cym and the immediate Lemma 8.6 antecedents (6.2), (6.6)–(6.7); I did not find a definition of the C_y^m norm in the supplied text. The context strongly indicates the usual supremum norm of torus derivatives through order m, but the paper excerpt does not formally specify that convention or whether it is a norm versus equivalent seminorm sum. Thus the Fourier summability argument is consistent under the standard convention, but an exact norm-dependent operator constant cannot be independently reconstructed from the stated pages alone.
- The “every fixed coefficient derivative” conclusion in the application is an order-by-order class estimate, not a single constant uniform over all derivative orders. (8.19) gives C_m orderwise; no uniformity in m is claimed. The source does not claim a bound uniform over varying choices of direction or schedule, which are fixed here.

Limits: this reviews the paper argument only; it does not verify any formal declaration or downstream implementation.
